sentences.sentence: Abstract:

A method is described for the identification of astaxanthin glucoside esters from snow alga Chlamydomonas nivalis by means of liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry with atmospheric pressure chemical ionization.

Astaxanthin, a carotenoid pigment with significant antioxidant properties, accumulates in the snow alga Chlamydomonas nivalis and plays a crucial role in its survival under extreme polar environments.
However, the presence of astaxanthin diglucoside diesters has not been previously documented in this organism.

In this study, we employed liquid chromatography coupled with atmospheric pressure chemical ionization mass spectrometry (LC-APCI-MS) to detect and identify astaxanthin glucoside esters present in extracts of Chlamydomonas nivalis.

By optimizing chromatographic and mass spectrometric conditions, we were able to separate and detect three novel astaxanthin diglucoside diester isomers, which we designated as Cn-ADA1, Cn-ADA2, and Cn-ADA3.

The molecular structures of these isomers were characterized by MS and MS/MS fragmentation patterns, demonstrating the presence of a diesterified glucoside moiety attached to the astaxanthin molecule.

Our results provide the first evidence of astaxanthin diglucoside diesters in Chlamydomonas nivalis and highlight the potential of LC-APCI-MS for the identification and characterization of complex carotenoid derivatives in algae.
Title: Primary resistance to single and multiple drugs in leprosy: a mouse footpad study.
Abstract:

Skin biopsy homogenates obtained from three cases of lepromatous leprosy with no prior history of antileprosy treatment were tested in the mouse footpad for the sensitivity of Mycobacterium leprae to multiple drugs.
This in vivo study aimed to assess the primary resistance of M. leprae to single and combination therapies commonly used in leprosy treatment.
Using a mouse footpad model, skin biopsy homogenates from lepromatous leprosy patients were injected into the hind footpads of C57BL/6 mice.
The mice were then treated with various antimycobacterial regimens, including rifampicin, clofazimine, and dapsone, alone or in combination.
The footpad swelling response, a surrogate marker of bacterial load and virulence, was measured at regular intervals following treatment initiation.
Our results showed that 66.7% of M. leprae isolates exhibited resistance to rifampicin, 44.4% to clofazimine, and 22.2% to dapsone as single agents.
Notably, 55.6% of isolates showed reduced susceptibility to the combination of rifampicin and clofazimine, indicating potential cross-resistance between these two drugs.
In contrast, the combination of rifampicin and dapsone showed a 20% reduction in footpad swelling, suggesting potential synergy between these drugs.
This study highlights the emergence of primary resistance to commonly used antimycobacterial agents in leprosy and underscores the need for careful surveillance of drug resistance patterns.

Furthermore, our findings emphasize the importance of preserving the efficacy of multidrug therapy (MDT) regimens in the treatment of leprosy, which is the cornerstone of leprosy control programs worldwide.
**Title:** Interplay of Family Traditions and Generations: An Exploratory Analysis of Intergenerational Transmission of Values
**Abstract:**
Currently, traditional family values that have been passed down through generations appear to be at risk.
This has significant implications for the stability and health of individuals, families, and communities.

This article explores selected issues related to intergenerational transmission of family values, focusing on the dynamics of family traditions and their impact on the well-being of subsequent generations.
Using a mixed-methods approach, we conducted a longitudinal study of 150 families across three generations.
Our data collection involved in-depth interviews, surveys, and observation of family interactions and rituals.
The results reveal that family traditions serve as a vital mechanism for transmitting values, skills, and social norms across generations.
Our findings indicate that families with strong, culturally relevant traditions tend to exhibit higher levels of cohesion, emotional intelligence, and social support among family members.
Conversely, families that have abandoned or distanced themselves from traditional practices often report increased conflict, emotional distress, and decreased sense of belonging.
The study also reveals that intergenerational transmission of values is influenced by various factors, including cultural background, socioeconomic status, and family structure.

Specifically, families from diverse cultural backgrounds tend to place greater emphasis on preserving traditional practices and values, while families from more privileged socioeconomic backgrounds may prioritize individualism and self-reliance over collectivist values.
This research highlights the critical role of family traditions in fostering social capital, promoting emotional well-being, and cultivating a sense of community among family members.
Our findings underscore the importance of preserving and revitalizing traditional family practices in the face of cultural and societal change.
As a member of the testis-specific serine/threonine protein kinase (TSSK) family, Tssk4 is exclusively expressed in the testis and plays an essential role in male fertility.
We previously reported that Tssk4 is involved in regulating the structure and function of sperm flagella, however the downstream targets of Tssk4 remain poorly understood.
In this study, we identify Odf2 as a novel substrate of Tssk4 and demonstrate that Tssk4 phosphorylates Odf2 at Ser-76.
Using a combination of biochemical and cell-based assays, we show that Tssk4 directly phosphorylates Odf2 in vitro and in vivo.
Phosphorylation of Odf2 at Ser-76 is dependent on Tssk4 activity, as demonstrated by the use of a Tssk4-specific inhibitor and a kinase-deficient Tssk4 mutant.
We also demonstrate that this phosphorylation event occurs in the context of the sperm axoneme, where Odf2 is a component of the outer doublet microtubules.
Furthermore, we show that phosphorylation of Odf2 at Ser-76 alters its subcellular localization and affects its interaction with other axonemal proteins.
These changes in Odf2 phosphorylation and localization are associated with changes in sperm motility, suggesting that Tssk4-mediated Odf2 phosphorylation plays a role in regulating sperm function.
Title: Collision Synthesis of Unique Carbon Nanomaterials Inspired by the Allende Meteorite
A simple shock event approach inspired by the Allende meteorite to produce sophisticated carbon nanomaterials is reported.
It is demonstrated that unique carbon nanostructures, including carbon nanotubes, carbon onions, and new carbon nanorings are synthesized through a low-temperature, high-pressure collision process.
The resulting carbon nanomaterials exhibit exceptional properties, including enhanced mechanical strength, high thermal conductivity, and unique optical behavior.
By mimicking the high-temperature and high-pressure conditions that occur during meteorite impacts, we have developed a novel method for producing complex carbon nanostructures.

Our experimental results show that the collision synthesis approach produces a diverse array of carbon nanoforms, including single-walled and multi-walled carbon nanotubes, fullerenes, and novel, ring-shaped carbon nanostructures.

Scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and Raman spectroscopy were employed to characterize the morphology, crystal structure, and chemical bonding of the synthesized carbon nanomaterials.
The results suggest that the collision synthesis process facilitates the rapid formation of large, ordered domains of carbon atoms, which give rise to the observed unique nanostructures.

This work represents a significant step forward in the development of novel methods for synthesizing complex carbon nanomaterials, with potential applications in fields such as energy storage, electronics, and biomedical devices.
The findings of this study also shed new light on the processes that occur during meteorite impacts, and provide valuable insights into the formation of extraterrestrial carbon-based materials.
**Title:** Guillain-Barré Syndrome as a Manifestation of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
Report of a Case.
**Abstract:**
The case of a young female patient with acute symmetrical ascending polyneuropathy as a manifestation of systemic lupus erythematosus is reported.
There was involvement of several cranial nerves and the cerebrospinal fluid showed elevated protein levels with a normal cell count.
Clinical presentation, electromyography (EMG) and nerve conduction studies (NCS) revealed a demyelinating pattern consistent with Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS).

Laboratory investigations confirmed a diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) with the presence of antinuclear antibodies (ANA), anti-SSA/Ro antibodies, and a low complement level (C3 55 mg/dL).

The patient responded well to immunosuppressive therapy with intravenous methylprednisolone and cyclophosphamide, alongside supportive care, resulting in significant improvement of her symptoms and neurological function.

This case highlights the unusual manifestation of SLE as GBS, a rare but serious complication that emphasizes the importance of considering autoimmune diseases in the differential diagnosis of GBS and vice versa.
The case report contributes to the expanding body of literature on the association between SLE and neurological manifestations.

**Title:** Effect of the Density of an Emulsion Explosive on the Reaction Zone Width
**Abstract:**

This paper presents experimental dependences of the width of the reaction zone and detonation critical diameter on the initial density with a variation in the density of an emulsion high explosive from 0.5 to 1.33 g/cm^3.
Glass beads of uniform size were used as the inert filler to ensure a consistent particle distribution and minimize the effects of density variability in the explosive matrix.
A shock tube was employed to generate spherical shock waves with overdriven conditions, which simulated the detonation process.
The width of the reaction zone was measured using high-speed Schlieren photography and analyzed in conjunction with spectroscopic data obtained using a streak camera.
Results showed a non-linear increase in the width of the reaction zone with an increase in the initial density of the emulsion explosive.
This behavior was attributed to the changes in the packing fraction of the explosive particles and the degree of confinement of the reaction zone.
Furthermore, the detonation critical diameter was found to decrease with an increase in the initial density, which was consistent with the expected trend for shock-sensitive energetic materials.
These findings have important implications for the design and optimization of emulsion explosives for specific applications, such as mining and demolition.

Title: A model of competitive airline revenue management interactions
Abstract:
In this article we develop a model of the interactions between the revenue management (RM) practices of competing airlines.
The theoretical model is supported by PODS simulation results that highlight the important role of passenger spill between airlines on RM seat allocations in competitive markets.

Our model captures the strategic behavior of airlines as they respond to changes in their competitors' RM strategies, resulting in dynamic and adaptive price setting, seat allocation, and demand segmentation.
We investigate the impact of various RM practices, including dynamic pricing, overbooking, and yield management, on airline revenue and passenger spill.

Our results demonstrate that, under competitive pressures, airlines tend to adopt strategies that prioritize price competition over yield maximization, leading to lower revenue and higher passenger spill.

Furthermore, we find that the effectiveness of RM strategies is significantly influenced by the presence of passenger spill, which can lead to a decrease in revenue and an increase in demand uncertainty.
Our findings have significant implications for the airline industry, where RM practices are critical to maintaining competitive advantage in the face of intense competition.

By providing insights into the interactions between RM practices and passenger spill, our model can inform more effective revenue management strategies that take into account the dynamic nature of competitive markets.
Abstract:
We investigated how people use base rates and sample size information when combining data to make overall probability judgments.
Participants considered two samples from an animal population in order to estimate the probability of that animal being aggressive.
Participants' judgments were influenced by subpopulation base rates, but only when one of the samples was deemed representative, and thus, reliable.

Notably, the perceived representativeness of the samples affected whether judgments were more influenced by the base rate of aggression in the population or the sample size of the aggressive individuals in the samples.

When samples were perceived as representative, judgments relied more heavily on the sample size information, whereas when samples were perceived as unrepresentative, judgments became more reliant on the population base rate.
This finding highlights the complexities of human reasoning and decision-making when combining statistical information.
Abstract
The photon decay of the relativistic Coulomb excitation of the double Giant Dipole Resonance (GDR) in the target has been observed in 1 AGeV 209 Bi on 208 Pb.
The photon spectrometer utilized in this experiment was capable of measuring high-energy photon emission with an unprecedented degree of precision.
In this study, we investigated the relativistic Coulomb excitation of the 2-phonon GDR in 208Pb through the analysis of electromagnetic decay products emitted during the collision.
A beam of 1 AGeV 209Bi ions was directed at a target of 208Pb, inducing nuclear excitations via Coulomb interaction.
The subsequent decay of the excited states was detected by a state-of-the-art photon spectrometer, enabling the measurement of high-energy gamma-ray spectra with excellent energy resolution.
The observed data reveal a clear peak at the predicted energy of the double GDR, confirming the relativistic Coulomb excitation of this collective state.

Furthermore, the analysis of photon yields and energy spectra allows for a quantitative determination of the 2-phonon GDR excitation probability, providing valuable insights into the dynamics of nuclear excitations at relativistic energies.
Our findings have important implications for the understanding of nuclear structure and reactions at high energies, and contribute to the advancement of nuclear physics research.
